<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Detecting deviations from normal operation in wind turbines is inherently challenging due to the trade-off between sensitivity to incipient faults and robustness to benign operational variability. Gradual degradation and measurement noise further obscure early fault signatures, motivating monitoring strategies that can detect subtle deviations associated with fault initiation at an early stage while limiting false alarms. Residual-based condition monitoring using Normal Behaviour Models (NBMs) addresses this challenge by identifying persistent deviations from a learned healthy baseline, but effective detection depends on both the NBM and how temporal patterns in the residuals are processed by anomaly detection (AD) algorithms. A key practical challenge is that the same AD algorithm can behave very differently depending on how the signal is modelled and transformed. This study investigates how AD behaviour and performance trade-offs change across modelling scenarios by comparing three data driven NBMs, Long Short-Term Memory, Convolutional Neural Network, and Feed-Forward Neural Network, combined with four AD approaches: a Statistical Control Chart, a two-sided Page Cumulative Sum procedure (CUSUM), Kolmogorov-Smirnov comparative detection (KSCAD), and Bayesian comparative detection (BCAD). A no-NBM baseline is included, where the raw target sensor signal is processed identically and supplied directly to the AD algorithms. The evaluation covers two fault families (rotor-bearing and generator-bearing), with paired healthy references, using SCADA cases from the CARE to Compare dataset. Performance is assessed using the CARE framework, which jointly evaluates fault coverage, accuracy during healthy operation, reliability, and detection earliness, enabling a structured comparison of sensitivity, robustness, stability, and responsiveness across cases. The results show that modelling decisions can substantially reshape detection behaviour, with different AD algorithms exhibiting distinct trade-offs in responsiveness and false alarm suppression depending on fault family and signal representation.</jats:p>
title: Detecting Changes in Normal Wind Turbine Operations Using Data Driven Approaches
